title: Ahmedabad to Host 2029 World Weightlifting Championships, a First for India
excerpt: The IWF Executive Board picked Ahmedabad over bids linked to Russia and Venezuela; the championships will double as a qualifying event for the 2030 Commonwealth Games.
body:
• Ahmedabad will host the 2029 IWF World Weightlifting Championships, the first time India stages the sport's senior world championships.
  • The IWF Executive Board made the award at its meeting in Ningbo, China, on Sunday, with India prevailing over competing interest from Russia and Venezuela.
  • The 2029 championships will also serve as a qualifying event for the 2030 Commonwealth Games, which Ahmedabad is scheduled to host.
  • Moscow gets the 2030 senior worlds; Prishtina hosts the 2028 youth championships and Caracas the 2028 junior championships.

India will host the senior World Weightlifting Championships for the first time in 2029, after the International Weightlifting Federation's Executive Board awarded the event to Ahmedabad at its meeting in Ningbo, China, on Sunday. The IWF announcement confirmed Ahmedabad for 2029 and Moscow for the 2030 senior edition, part of a single decision awarding four world championships between 2028 and 2030.

"It's a big day for Indian weightlifting as the IWF world championships will be coming to India for the first time and will be organised in Ahmedabad. Russia and Venezuela had strongly pitched for the 2029 championships but the IWF Executive Board has put faith in India."

— Sahdev Yadav, President, Indian Weightlifting Federation

A Gujarat runway built over three years

The award extends a deliberate build-up in Gujarat. Ahmedabad hosted the 2025 Commonwealth Weightlifting Championships, and India staged the 2026 Asian Senior Weightlifting Championships at the Mahatma Mandir Convention and Exhibition Centre in Gandhinagar from May 11 to 17, drawing athletes and officials from nearly 30 countries, according to IANS reporting. Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi announced the decision on X, writing that after the Commonwealth and Asian championships, "the world's best weightlifters are now coming to Gujarat."

The 2029 worlds carry competitive weight beyond prestige: they will serve as a qualifying event for the 2030 Commonwealth Games, which India is scheduled to host in Ahmedabad. Yadav said that gives Indian lifters a home-platform route to Commonwealth berths. Ahmedabad is also India's proposed host city in its 2036 Olympic bid.

First-time hosts across the calendar

IWF General Secretary José Quiñones noted that three of the four chosen hosts — India, Kosovo and Venezuela — will organise an IWF world event for the first time. Prishtina will stage the 2028 World Youth Championships and Caracas the 2028 World Junior Championships. "All the bids we received were excellent," Quiñones said, adding that the spread of hosts "demonstrates our sport is growing worldwide." The federation said awarding four championships together was meant to consolidate and streamline its international calendar.

What happens next

The announcement came on the sidelines of this year's World Championships in Ningbo, which start on Tuesday and double as the first qualification tournament for the LA 2028 Olympics. A seven-member Indian team, including Tokyo Olympic silver medallist Mirabai Chanu — now lifting in the 53kg class after the Olympic weight-class restructuring — is competing there. Her results over the next three seasons will shape the squad India fields when the worlds come home in 2029.
